::: {.callout-note}
This is an illustrative public draft for testing the reference format. It has not been adopted as a recommended OWAS standard.
:::

## Definition

Count distinct people with at least one qualifying employment spell active at reference instant *t*. Count each person once within the reporting population.

## Population and unit

Unit: people. The illustrative population includes employees and excludes independent contractors. Document legal entities, worker classes, and leave treatment before using this definition.

## Time basis

Use an inclusive start and exclusive end: `start <= t` and (`end` is missing or `t < end`). State the timezone and whether the source stores dates or timestamps. A missing end means ongoing only when that is the source system's documented convention.

## Calculation

Filter qualifying spells at *t*, then count distinct stable person identifiers. Do not sum assignment rows.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS headcount
FROM employment_spells
WHERE start_at <= :reference_instant
  AND (end_at IS NULL OR :reference_instant < end_at);
```

Apply population filters before this query. `:reference_instant` is a conceptual parameter; adapt syntax to the database.

## Required data

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| person_id | Stable identifier across qualifying spells |
| start_at | Inclusive spell start |
| end_at | Exclusive spell end, or documented ongoing marker |
| worker_class | Population eligibility |
| entity_id | Reporting scope |

## Worked example

At 09:00, A has two active assignments, B has one active spell, and C has a spell ending at 09:00. With the boundary rule above, headcount is **2**: A and B.

## Validation

Check missing person IDs, reversed intervals, duplicate spells, and unexpected changes by entity. Reconcile person-level differences against the prior snapshot before interpreting the aggregate.

## Limitations

This is not full-time equivalent capacity or an average over a period. Late corrections can change historical counts. Record both the effective instant and the extraction date for reproducibility.

## Sources and review

Original illustrative example; no external standard is claimed. Open questions include leave eligibility, multi-entity attribution, and date-only termination conventions.
